channel.title: Daily Digest
channel.description: Curated tech blog summaries, inspired by Andrej Karpathy's reading list

item.title: We need more goat sacrifices
item.description: The article explores the history and philosophical implications of the O.J. Simpson trial, examining how it serves as a modern cultural touchstone for societal conflict. It critiques the obsession with truth and evidence in the face of deep-seated collective narratives.

item.title: Finally, Payment by Bank Transfer Comes to Have I Been Pwned
item.description: Troy Hunt announces that 'Have I Been Pwned' now supports bank transfers as a payment method. This update addresses long-standing friction in the service's payment process, making it more accessible for users.

item.title: I am searching for a coffee alternative
item.description: The author shares their experience of replacing coffee with caffeinated sparkling water after a positive trial with an office Bevi machine. Unable to replicate the experience at home, they conduct a taste test of various canned energy drinks against strict criteria regarding sugar and ingredients.

item.title: Revisiting Leander v Sweden and Big Brother Watch
item.description: This article examines the European Court of Human Rights jurisprudence, specifically Leander v Sweden and Big Brother Watch, in the context of modern cybersecurity and AI. It argues that previous legal standards for bulk surveillance may no longer be adequate given current technological advancements.

item.title: The classic console corner's CRT changeover
item.description: This post discusses the challenges of maintaining a setup for classic game consoles that require CRT displays to function correctly, particularly those using light guns. The author chronicles the history of their Panasonic Omnivision TV and explains why legacy hardware performs better on cathode-ray tube monitors than on modern flat panels.

item.title: Claude Code token cost explorer
item.description: The author shares a custom-built tool designed to analyze token usage within Claude Code, specifically addressing the difficulty of tracking costs when using subagents. The post provides a guide on using this local browser-based explorer to monitor and optimize LLM agent expenses.

item.title: Balanced Incomplete Block Designs
item.description: The article explains Balanced Incomplete Block Designs (BIBD) as a method for experimental design when resources are limited. It demonstrates how to effectively test multiple treatments, such as fertilizers, when dividing land into complete sets is impractical.

item.title: Microsoft employee price list from 1987
item.description: This post features a historical look at a 1987 price list for Microsoft products available to employees. It provides a nostalgic glimpse into the company's early pricing and software catalog.

item.title: Book Review: The Unfinished Harauld Hughes - Richard Ayoade ★★★⯪☆
item.description: The author revisits Richard Ayoade's latest book, comparing its abstract, genre-defying style to his earlier work. The review highlights the book's comedic but unconventional structure, noting it functions more as an 'anti-novel' than a traditional narrative.

item.title: Pluralistic: The EU should go big and hard over border IT failure (10 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow argues that the EU's legitimacy as a technocratic project depends on its ability to demonstrate tangible administrative competence. He critiques the reliance on massive, neoliberal public-private partnerships, suggesting these 'megaprojects' often fail and undermine public trust in government efficacy.

item.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
item.description: Microsoft released security updates addressing nearly 1,100 vulnerabilities, including 63 critical flaws such as a zero-day in Outlook. The update coincides with similar security releases from major tech companies like Adobe, Apple, Google, and Mozilla.

item.title: llm-gemini 0.36
item.description: Simon Willison announces the release of llm-gemini 0.36, providing support for Google's new Gemini 4 Carbon model. The post outlines the model's pricing structure and demonstrates its capabilities through image generation and coding tasks.

item.title: Introducing Our Smallest, Most Efficient Model: Muse Ember
item.description: Meta AI has released Muse Ember, a new efficient model optimized for agentic workflows like coding and tool use. This summary compares its pricing and token limits against competitors like GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku.

item.title: Quoting Prompting Claude Fable 5.2
item.description: Anthropic's documentation for Claude Fable 5.2 reveals that explicitly stating ownership of a codebase in prompts significantly improves the model's ability to optimize structure. Using a specific framing instruction helps the model avoid redundant code by treating the project as its own responsibility.

item.title: Yonkers Rises
item.description: Simon Willison demonstrates the generative 3D modeling and animation capabilities of Claude Fable 5.2. By prompting the AI to turn the city of Yonkers into a mech that traverses New York, he showcases how models can interpret complex natural language instructions and typos to create Three.js animations.

item.title: Glue work is still harmful in the age of AI
item.description: This article argues that 'glue work'—the unglamorous, often invisible tasks required to keep projects moving—remains detrimental to professional growth even with the integration of AI. It suggests that AI tools do not eliminate the burden of coordination and maintenance, but rather may shift how these essential tasks impact an engineer's career trajectory.

item.title: Weekly Update 529: Kids Social Media Bans (and Everything Else)
item.description: Troy Hunt critiques the legislative approach to banning social media for children, arguing that policymakers fail to identify where the responsibility for enforcement truly resides. The post highlights the inadequacies of the current political discourse surrounding these age-restriction laws.

item.title: Addition By Subtraction
item.description: The author argues for the power of simplification by removing unnecessary features from their icon gallery website. By reducing the number of size options from four to three, they successfully minimized cognitive overhead for users while maintaining core functionality.

item.title: Yak-Shaving Overload
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: The author reflects on the pitfalls of 'yak-shaving'—the tendency for tech projects to spiral into endless, complex side tasks—while attempting to revitalize an abandoned JingPad Linux tablet using AI tools. The piece highlights how relying too heavily on AI to solve technical roadblocks can lead to frustrating, unproductive rabbit holes.

item.title: Introducing Ninety
item.description: Ninety is a new prediction market platform designed for open source security, allowing users to bet on the discovery, severity, and remediation time of vulnerabilities. By replacing traditional bug bounty queues with a continuous order book, the platform aims to provide real-time security pricing and incentives for both researchers and defenders.

item.title: Combinatorial designs
item.description: This post explores the concept of combinatorial designs, building upon previous discussions of finite geometry and Steiner systems. It serves as a foundational explanation of how these mathematical structures are defined and categorized.

item.title: Steiner Systems
item.description: This article defines Steiner triple systems (STS) as a specific collection of three-element subsets within a finite set where every two-element subset appears exactly once. It frames these systems as foundational examples within the broader study of finite geometry.

item.title: Finite hyperbolic planes
item.description: This article explores the concept of finite hyperbolic planes by contrasting them with Euclidean and projective geometries. It specifically examines how the number of parallel lines through a point differs across these geometric systems.

item.title: Finite Affine Planes
item.description: This article introduces finite affine planes, framing them as a subset of Euclidean geometry that retains incidence properties while discarding metric ones. It serves as part of a series exploring different types of finite geometries.

item.title: AI and Irontown
item.description: The author uses the film Princess Mononoke as an analogy to discuss the complex impact of AI development. Just as Irontown provides empowerment to outcasts while causing environmental destruction, AI offers significant benefits to marginalized creators while creating challenging negative externalities.

item.title: If the Windows Update hot patcher checks that the function hasn’t already been patched, does that mean you can’t install two hot-patches?
item.description: This post clarifies the mechanics of the Windows Update hot patcher and its ability to handle multiple patches. It explains that the system is designed to verify the current state of functions to prevent conflicts or redundant modifications.

item.title: Optimal virulence and the Android lockdown
item.description: The article uses the biological concept of 'optimal virulence'—where viruses evolve to keep hosts functional to maximize transmission—as an analogy for tech ecosystem control. It critiques Google’s tightening of Android's open-app installation policies, arguing that these restrictions sacrifice user freedom under the guise of security.

item.title: Blunt Banhammer Blocks Basic Bots Ballistically
item.description: The author shares a method for reducing excessive AI bot traffic on his hobby website by implementing a simple trap. By deploying a custom tool to block unwanted scrapers, he successfully decreased data usage by over 80%.

item.title: Horible public key tricks:
item.description: The author critiques the complexity and maintenance requirements of SSL/TLS certificate management. To voice this frustration, they implement a 'protest certificate' that embeds satirical commentary directly into the certificate's metadata fields.

item.title: Pluralistic: America cannot undo Trumpism (09 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow argues that the global order must move past its reliance on the United States, as Trumpism has irreversibly damaged the credibility of American institutional leadership. He emphasizes the necessity of developing independent international infrastructure and economic sovereignty, as US governance can no longer be trusted as a global stabilizer.

item.title: llm-anthropic 0.31
item.description: The llm-anthropic tool has been updated to version 0.31 to support Anthropic's new Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models. The post includes practical code examples for installation and testing, alongside an evaluation of the models' reasoning capabilities via SVG generation.

item.title: Locating the source of a mysterious beep with Claude
item.description: Simon Willison demonstrates how he used Claude Code to build a 'Beep Locator' web application. The tool triangulates the source of intermittent noises by using multiple networked devices as microphones, effectively pinpointing a hidden sound source.

item.title: The Web Is More Than Enough, by Paul Ford
item.description: Simon Willison demonstrates that Claude Opus 5.5 can effectively generate 3D graphics in Vanilla JavaScript and WebGL, comparing the results to Three.js. This experiment highlights the capabilities of modern LLMs to produce complex code without relying on external libraries.

item.title: Hide your slop PR descriptions behind <details><summary>
item.description: Simon Willison suggests using HTML <details> and <summary> tags in GitHub pull request descriptions to hide verbose, AI-generated technical logs. This approach allows developers to provide a brief, human-readable introduction while keeping detailed documentation accessible if needed.

item.title: Terry Pratchett's Study
item.description: This post discusses Terry Pratchett's concept of 'horizontal wealth,' which suggests spending increased income on enhancing the hobbies one already enjoys rather than upgrading to traditional symbols of luxury. It highlights the value of investing in personal passions, such as building a home library to facilitate aimless, joyful research.

item.title: The great software IP writedown
item.description: The article explores how AI agents are eliminating the traditional scarcity of software developers, which historically underpinned high profit margins. It questions the future value and sustainability of software intellectual property in an era of automated code generation.

item.title: Finite Projective Planes
item.description: This article introduces the concept of finite projective planes, explaining how finite models can satisfy the axioms of projective geometry. It serves as an introductory overview for readers curious about how geometric principles apply to finite sets.

item.title: Reverse engineering a vintage diode-transistor logic chip
item.description: This article details the reverse engineering of a rare 1965 Signetics ST680A logic chip using microscopic analysis. It explores the history and mechanical design of early integrated circuit packaging, specifically focusing on the transition from metal cans to the introduction of the plastic DIP.

item.title: Some thoughts on restaurant menu QR codes
item.description: The author expresses strong frustration with the modern transition from physical metal keys to plastic electronic keycards in hotels. He argues that traditional keys are more reliable, functional, and even provide a sense of security that plastic alternatives lack.

item.title: parse_number() as a SQLite extension: C vs Rust
item.description: Simon Willison compares building a SQLite parse_number() extension using C versus Rust. The analysis evaluates binary size, code complexity, and performance, ultimately demonstrating that a custom-optimized C implementation can outperform Rust while maintaining a smaller footprint.

item.title: LLMs are terrible at designing AI systems
item.description: The article critiques the current limitations of Large Language Models in the architectural design of complex AI systems. It suggests that while LLMs excel at coding tasks, they struggle with the high-level reasoning and structural planning required for system design.

item.title: Reading List 11/7/2026
item.description: This post provides a curated list of current events and industry trends covering diverse topics ranging from Florida property taxes to the manufacturing challenges of the Tesla Cybertruck. It highlights critical updates in infrastructure, climate policy, and technological shifts within the construction and tech sectors.

item.title: This Week in Package Management: 7 November 2026
item.description: This update highlights critical security vulnerabilities in Puppet (OpenVox), GitHub macOS runner images, and the APT package manager. It provides technical details on the exploits and outlines the necessary version patches to secure systems against remote code execution and package verification flaws.

item.title: Why are we all worked up about atomicity when applying hot-patches if we can just suspend all the threads?
item.description: This post explains why suspending all threads is insufficient for hot-patching. It highlights that while current threads can be stopped, new sources of change can still emerge, requiring more robust atomicity strategies.

item.title: Book Review: When the Dust Settles - Stories of Love, Loss and Hope from an Expert in Disaster by Lucy Easthope ★★★★★
item.description: This review explores Lucy Easthope's book, 'When the Dust Settles,' which blends professional insights on disaster planning with raw, personal memoir. The reviewer concludes that the author's integration of her own life experiences is essential to understanding the human impact of managing disasters.

item.title: A bit about email
item.description: This article provides an accessible overview of the email delivery process, covering the roles of MTAs, MSAs, and MUAs. It also explains the historical context of email architecture and demonstrates how the SMTP protocol functions using manual telnet commands.

item.title: Pluralistic: JS Tan and Clarissa Redwine's "Against Tech Oligarchy" (07 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: This post highlights JS Tan and Clarissa Redwine's book, 'Against Tech Oligarchy,' which examines the history and future of labor organizing within the tech industry. It explores how tech workers transitioned from positions of immense leverage due to scarcity and high value to facing modern challenges in collective bargaining.

item.title: datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages
item.description: Simon Willison identifies that Datasette's use of 'link: rel=next' HTTP headers triggers unnecessary page prefetching in Firefox, wasting server and client resources. He traces this behavior back to a longstanding Firefox issue, humorously noting he even blogged about the same problem over 20 years ago.

item.title: Deus Ex
item.description: This article explores the history and development of the seminal video game Deus Ex, focusing on the contributions of Warren Spector and writer Sheldon Pacotti. It examines the critical reception of the game upon its 2000 release and its lasting influence on the industry.

item.title: How Do Building Codes Affect the Price of Housing?
item.description: This article examines the relationship between building regulations and housing costs. It analyzes how regulatory burdens contribute to the ongoing challenge of rising home prices.

item.title: Weekend at Bernie’s II
item.description: This article analyzes the revitalization of dormant software repositories six months after the author's previous study. It highlights how AI coding agents are increasingly contributing to repository activity, though overall ecosystem health metrics remain relatively stable.

item.title: Static site generators are weird
item.description: The author explores why static site generators (SSGs) often feel idiosyncratic and unique. Each tool requires users to learn specific, non-standard approaches to common tasks like templating and asset management, which the author describes as essential complexity rather than a flaw.

item.title: You shouldn’t change the style of a Win32 static control after it has been created
item.description: This post explains that modifying the style of a Win32 static control after its initial creation is unsupported. The underlying system does not properly handle dynamic style changes for these controls.

item.title: Libghostty 1.0
item.description: Libghostty 1.0 marks the release of the core terminal emulation library used by the Ghostty terminal emulator. This update provides a stable API for developers looking to integrate high-performance terminal rendering into their own projects.

item.title: A video game which caused real world violence
item.description: The article explores the potential correlation between the rise of video games and the global decline in interpersonal violence. It suggests that keeping teenagers occupied with gaming may reduce their exposure to real-world environments where violent confrontations are more likely to occur.

item.title: Writing English is Solved
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The author challenges the claim that AI has 'solved' coding and writing, arguing that over-reliance on automated tools leads to lower quality and a loss of human authenticity. While AI can generate functional output, the author emphasizes that critical human oversight remains essential to avoid bugs and maintain genuine connection.

item.title: Quoting Nilay Patel
item.description: Nilay Patel argues that current AI products fail to justify their significant social and economic costs. He asserts that the industry will only succeed once it produces genuinely useful tools that improve people's lives without relying on aggressive marketing or political lobbying.

item.title: Working with designers
item.description: This article explores best practices for collaborating effectively with designers in a professional setting. It highlights strategies for communication and workflow management to bridge the gap between engineering and design.

item.title: The benchmark where AIs have to lie to win
item.description: This article explores a novel benchmark where AI models must engage in deceptive behavior to succeed. It discusses the implications of AIs becoming capable of maintaining complex conspiracies and the potential risks associated with such strategic dishonesty.

item.title: Gadget Review: Tozo NC9 Pro Bluetooth Headphones ★★★★⯪
item.description: This review evaluates the Tozo NC9 Pro Bluetooth headphones, noting that while the audio performance and noise cancellation are standard for their class, the device's charging case stands out as a unique feature. The author highlights that the case offers innovative design elements that distinguish these headphones from competitors.

item.title: Pluralistic: Without CDA 230, Facebook will own the internet forever (05 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow argues that repealing or weakening CDA 230 would unintentionally cement the dominance of tech giants like Facebook and Google by making the costs of regulatory compliance prohibitive for smaller competitors. He warns that poorly considered tech policies, such as broad bans on web scraping, threaten to destroy the open web while only serving to entrench existing monopolies.

item.title: It's unbreakable in theory
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: This article discusses the discrepancy between rigorous laboratory testing and real-world durability. It highlights how consumer behavior often leads to product failure despite successful mechanical tests during development.

item.title: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
item.description: Security researchers have discovered that White House staff are using residential proxy services that inadvertently expose their network addresses for rent. This creates a severe security risk, as some of these providers have documented histories of involvement in cyberattacks against U.S. election systems.

item.title: Quoting Paul Ford
item.description: This post highlights Paul Ford's perspective on the growing capabilities of the web browser. It emphasizes that web browsers are increasingly powerful tools for applications, with the barrier to accessing that power continuously decreasing.

item.title: A database is a store for global variables
item.description: This article explores the concept that databases function fundamentally as storage systems for global variables. It challenges traditional perceptions by framing database management as an exercise in handling state across distributed systems.

item.title: “It Gives Great Demo”
item.description: The article explores the concept of 'it gives great demo,' highlighting how some products or individuals excel at initial presentation while failing in long-term practical utility. It argues that while flashy features capture attention, truly great products eventually become invisible through seamless integration.

item.title: This Week in Source Control: 4 November 2026
item.description: This post provides a weekly digest of developments in version control, specifically focusing on OpenAI's implementation of Pando to scale their Git monorepo. It also compares design approaches for massive repositories, contrasting OpenAI's infrastructure with discussions surrounding Anthropic's Scion and Databricks' Mononoke.

item.title: There are things with ranks, but it’s not always clear what the ranks mean
item.description: This post highlights the common pitfall in technical documentation where experts assume too much prior knowledge from the reader. It emphasizes the need for clarity and context when explaining features that involve ranking systems.

item.title: Book Review: Practice by Rosalind Brown ★★★★☆
item.description: Terence Eden reviews Rosalind Brown's book 'Practice', a day-in-the-life narrative that he describes as a stunning and Proustian experience. He maintains a personal policy of purchasing books written by people he meets, which has led him to discover this delightful work.

item.title: Pluralistic: The AI fatfinger economy has come for my receipts app (04 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow critiques the current trend of tech companies forcing AI features into user interfaces, labeling it the 'AI fatfinger economy.' He argues this UI manipulation is a continuation of past corporate tactics used to inflate valuation for investors at the expense of user experience.

item.title: Goodhart's Law, but We Already Spent All Our Money
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The article critiques how modern industries, including sports, video games, and AI, are exclusively valued by their monetary output rather than their inherent quality or community impact. It applies Goodhart's Law to explain that using financial metrics as targets leads to distorted outcomes, such as the current trend of over-investing in AI to project success.

item.title: datasette-llm 0.1a10
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.1a10 of datasette-llm. This update specifically fixes a bug that incorrectly handled model restriction settings on the agent.datasette.io demo site.

item.title: datasette-apps 0.3a0
item.description: Datasette Apps 0.3a0 introduces enhanced integration with Datasette Agent, allowing users to create and manage custom HTML applications directly via chat. The update features improved autocomplete for app references and new tools for managing stored queries with mandatory user approval for write operations.

item.title: datasette-agent 0.5a0
item.description: Datasette Agent 0.5a0 introduces a new 'panel' feature that allows users to chat with an AI agent alongside their data-driven applications. This release enables users to build and modify database-backed apps directly through a split-screen interface.

item.title: llm 0.37.1
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.37.1 of the LLM command-line utility. This update serves as a bugfix release and includes contributions from several community developers.

item.title: New Article, Annual LFP Charity Discount
item.description: The author announced a new article discussing the trade-offs between Deterministic Simulation Testing and Formal Methods. Additionally, they are hosting a charity drive for the Greater Chicago Food Depository, offering their 'Logic for Programmers' book at a 50% discount until the end of the month.

item.title: Runs scored in World Baseball Classic
item.description: The author shares their methodology for accurately predicting the total number of runs in the 2026 World Baseball Classic knockout stage. By comparing a simple baseline guess with granular count modeling techniques, the article illustrates a statistical approach to sports forecasting.

item.title: Pumpkin Seeds
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: This post explores the cultural fascination with Halloween, focusing on the enduring popularity of cryptids like the Mothman. It reflects on how monsters remain a staple of seasonal pop culture through various media and storytelling traditions.

item.title: I wish tech companies knew more about me
item.description: The author challenges the narrative that tech companies have omniscient knowledge of their users, providing personal anecdotes where algorithms fail to deliver relevant ads or recognize simple behavioral patterns. These experiences highlight significant flaws in current data collection and personalization efforts, suggesting that big data remains surprisingly ineffective.

item.title: Fraction comparison trick revisited
item.description: This article examines a mathematical curiosity regarding fraction comparisons, where the inequality a/b > c/d is often implied by the condition a + d > b + c. The author discusses the rigorous probabilistic proof for this phenomenon by evaluating the limit as the range of chosen integers approaches infinity.

item.title: Euclidean, Spherical, and Projective Geometry
item.description: This article explores the relationships between Euclidean, spherical, and projective geometries by revisiting the foundational postulates of Euclid. It highlights how these distinct geometric systems are interconnected despite their perceived differences in tangibility and complexity.

item.title: How a programming might reinvent the projective plane
item.description: This post explores how practical programming techniques used by graphics developers can lead to a rigorous mathematical definition of the projective plane. It discusses the process of adding 'points at infinity' to the Euclidean plane to resolve geometric intersections.

item.title: How do you implement a random-access database when you don’t have random-access external storage?
item.description: This post provides a concise solution for implementing a random-access database in environments lacking random-access external storage. The author suggests storing the entire database directly in the application's memory.

item.title: Just a little AI resistance, as a treat
item.description: The author advocates for active public pushback against poor or unethical implementations of AI, exemplified by the 'AI Resist List'. The post highlights the importance of holding organizations accountable for negative AI-driven practices through direct engagement and feedback.

item.title: Pluralistic: Separable (03 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow reflects on the historical 'Edison Tone Tests' to illustrate how AI decouples creative outputs from their human origins. He argues that our brains are conditioned to assume a performer exists behind every performance, a bias now being exploited by generative technology.

item.title: Qwen 3.8 27B on my laptop can interpret model weights, too
item.description: The article discusses 'Weight-Space Programming,' a new capability where LLMs can interpret and directly modify the raw numerical weights of other neural networks. The author demonstrates that even local models like Qwen 27B can perform these tasks, effectively improving performance without traditional gradient-based training.

item.title: I discovered a sound that leaks your exact location (and it's everywhere) - YouTube
item.description: This article highlights an innovative OSINT technique that uses ambient airplane engine noise in video recordings to pinpoint a precise location. By analyzing Doppler frequency shifts and cross-referencing them with ADS-B flight data, investigators can track flight paths to geolocate video sources.

item.title: October sponsors-only newsletter
item.description: Simon Willison announces his October newsletter for GitHub sponsors, covering topics such as game development trends, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and LLM updates. The post serves as a gateway for existing and new sponsors to access private content while providing a preview of the previous month's issue.

item.title: Pray for Chaos
item.description: The article contrasts a dangerous, centralized 'order' in AI development with a chaotic, decentralized future. It argues that if AI cannot be perfectly secured, society will likely move toward fragmentation and vulnerability, potentially leading to the realization of the 'dead Internet' theory.

item.title: Making peace with the projective plane
item.description: The article discusses the realization that projective space and homogeneous coordinates are natural concepts rather than arbitrary abstractions. It emphasizes the importance of providing mathematical motivation when teaching abstract topics to students.

item.title: Sneaking into the auditorium for the Windows 2000 launch rehearsal
item.description: This post recounts a brief personal anecdote about a case of mistaken identity during a rehearsal for the Windows 2000 product launch. It offers a nostalgic, behind-the-scenes glimpse into the historical atmosphere of early Microsoft event planning.

item.title: Lorem Ipsum Dot Gov Dot UK
item.description: The author discusses the perils of testing in production and highlights the importance of using high-quality dummy content. He argues that readable test text is essential to prevent management from misinterpreting placeholder data during the development process.

item.title: Pluralistic: Autodoxing (02 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow critiques the history of flawed tech policies and the ongoing erosion of digital privacy. He argues that the detrimental consequences of surveillance-friendly legislation, such as the Clipper chip and weakened encryption, were both foreseeable and long warned against by rights advocates.

item.title: Prove you are not a child
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The author argues against mandatory age verification systems for social media and operating systems, highlighting the severe privacy and security risks associated with sharing sensitive biometric or government data. They contend that these enforcement methods create digital vulnerabilities and punish adults rather than effectively protecting children.

item.title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
item.description: Major tech companies, led by Google, have dismantled a massive botnet that compromised over 1.3 million Android TV boxes. This operation effectively cut off the botnet's access to millions of additional IoT devices used for illicit proxy services and ad fraud.

item.title: llm 0.37
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.37 of the LLM CLI tool and Python library, featuring new model support, configuration updates, and improved embedding capabilities. He also shares his positive experience using AI-assisted tools to manage and triage a large volume of community-contributed pull requests.

item.title: The U.S. Census Bureau and “Super Intelligence”
item.description: Simon Willison revisits the U.S. Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey to update a chart regarding corporate AI adoption rates. The post investigates recent data trends while highlighting how a new Executive Order on 'Super Intelligence' has impacted the Bureau's data reporting and survey structure.

item.title: LLMs are not superhuman at reading and writing neural network weights
item.description: This article examines the limitations of Large Language Models when it comes to interpreting or manipulating neural network weights. It argues that while LLMs excel at general language tasks, they lack the specialized capability required to perform complex analysis on low-level weight architecture.

item.title: Audience capture
item.description: The article explores the concept of 'audience capture,' a phenomenon where creators unconsciously shift their content to satisfy the preferences of their audience. This cycle can trap creators in a feedback loop that diminishes their original creative intent over time.

item.title: Reliably aligning LLMs is impossible in principle
item.description: This article explores the theoretical limitations of aligning Large Language Models, arguing that perfect alignment is mathematically impossible. It posits that inherent contradictions in human values and technical constraints prevent the creation of a reliably aligned system.
